description: A wildfire is approaching a semi-urban settlement. Focus on preparedness, evacuation timing, and safety — not on fighting the fire yourself.
objectives: Assess wildfire warnings and wind direction correctly
Prepare defensible space and an emergency kit
Evacuate before routes are cut off

steps.title: Smoke on the Horizon
steps.narrative: You see smoke a few kilometres away and hear a wildfire is spreading in dry, windy conditions. No evacuation order yet.

options.text: Prepare an emergency kit, clear flammable material near your home, and monitor official updates
Assume it's far enough away and carry on as normal
options.mistake: Wildfires can move very fast when wind-driven — early preparation buys critical time later.

options.text: Go closer to see how bad it is
options.mistake: Approaching an active wildfire is dangerous and provides no safety benefit.

steps.title: Wind Shift
steps.narrative: The wind shifts and now blows toward the settlement, pushing the fire in your direction faster than expected.

options.text: Treat this as your cue to finalize evacuation readiness immediately
Wait for an official evacuation order before doing anything further
options.mistake: Waiting passively when conditions clearly worsen can cost you your evacuation window.

steps.title: Evacuation Order
steps.narrative: An evacuation order is issued for your zone. You have a family member with limited mobility.

options.text: Evacuate immediately, helping your family member and taking your emergency kit
Try to stay and defend the house yourself with a garden hose
options.mistake: Untrained residents should never attempt to fight a large wildfire — evacuation is the safe choice.

options.text: Delay leaving until you're fully certain it's necessary
options.mistake: Delaying evacuation after an official order risks routes being cut off by fire or smoke.

steps.title: Choosing a Route
steps.narrative: One evacuation route runs through an area with heavy smoke and low visibility; another is longer but clearer.

options.text: Take the longer, clearer route even though it takes more time
Take the smoky shortcut to save time
options.mistake: Driving through heavy smoke drastically reduces visibility and increases accident and inhalation risk.

steps.title: On the Road
steps.narrative: Embers are visibly landing near the road ahead. Traffic has slowed. What's the safest approach?

options.text: Keep windows up, use recirculated air, and follow official traffic directions calmly
Get out of the car to see what's causing the slowdown
options.mistake: Exiting your vehicle near active embers and heavy traffic is unnecessary and increases exposure risk.

steps.title: Reaching Safety
steps.narrative: You arrive at a designated safe zone away from the fire.

options.text: Check in with officials, and wait for an official all-clear before considering returning home
Head back home as soon as the smoke looks a little lighter
options.mistake: Returning before an official all-clear risks encountering active fire, hot spots, or blocked roads.
